name: Prepare and submit a stipulated price tender
summary: A stipulated price tender is a sealed lump-sum bid for a building designed by the owner's consultant, usually a school, hospital wing, university or municipal building. Over a three to five week tender period estimators read the documents, visit the site, take off and price the self-performed concrete and carpentry, price general conditions, follow addenda, obtain a bid bond and agreement to bond, and on closing day carry the best trade prices and submit a bid that must be complete and unqualified. Most of the price comes from trade quotes that arrive in the last hours, so the final day is rushed and error-prone, and a missed addendum or bond detail makes the bid non-compliant. About one bid in six to ten wins.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian national general contractor with about $1.5B of annual construction revenue, an Ontario head office and regional offices in Western and Atlantic Canada, bidding public and private institutional, commercial and industrial buildings.
baseline.notes: Bids submitted electronically on owner portals by 2020-2022, with paper bids still used by some owners in 2019; digital bonds spread in the same years. Estimating uses take-off software and Excel bid summaries.

trigger: The go/no-go meeting approves a stipulated price tender and the tender package is handed to estimating.
end_state: The bid is submitted and the result is known: low bidder going to contract award, not low, withdrawn for error, rejected, or not submitted.

volume.seasonality: Peak from February to June when public owners tender capital work before and after the fiscal year-end; quiet in December.

evidence.note: Organisation file estimate for bd-stipulated-bid (15-22-32 a month).

steps.name: Open the bid file
steps.description: The bid coordinator opens the bid folder handed over from the go decision, checks that all drawings, specifications and addenda issued so far are downloaded, and sets up the bid summary workbook from the company template.

error.defect_description: A drawing volume or early addendum is missing from the bid folder.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; template-driven bid set-up.

steps.name: Read the documents and plan the estimate
steps.description: The lead estimator reads the instructions to bidders, bid form, specifications and drawings, lists the trade packages, self-performed scopes, alternates and separate prices, and agrees the estimate plan and deadlines with the chief estimator.

error.defect_description: A specification section or separate price on the bid form is missed in the plan.

evidence.note: Contents of solicitation documents (scope, bid form, separate prices, subcontractor list) from the source; times are estimates.

steps.name: Issue trade packages for pricing
steps.description: The bid coordinator sends the trade package list to trade tendering so that invitations go to prequalified subcontractors and suppliers, about 25 to 35 packages per bid.

error.defect_description: A package is left off the list and has no coverage.

evidence.note: A large building bid has 25 or more scope packages.

steps.name: Send the tender terms for legal review
steps.description: The lead estimator emails the agreement, supplementary conditions and insurance and bonding requirements to contracts counsel and asks for a short memo on liability, liquidated damages, indemnities and payment terms before the bid is priced.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; the organisation file links this process to legal-prime-contract-review.

steps.name: Attend the site visit
steps.description: The lead estimator drives to the owner's site for the scheduled or mandatory site meeting, signs in, wears the owner's required protective equipment, and notes access, staging space, existing conditions and occupied areas that affect general conditions and phasing.

error.defect_description: A site constraint (access, hoarding, live services) is not recorded.

control.basis: Owner site rules and the company health and safety program: sign-in, PPE and escort on occupied sites

evidence.note: Site visit dates and mandatory attendance are set in the tender notice; time is an estimate.

steps.name: Take off self-performed quantities
steps.description: The estimator measures concrete, formwork, reinforcing, carpentry and general labour quantities from the drawings in the take-off software and checks them against the structural notes and specifications.

error.defect_description: A quantity is mis-measured or a drawing area is omitted.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; self-perform concrete and carpentry are in the organisation file.

steps.name: Price self-performed work
steps.description: The estimator applies crew compositions, productivity rates and unit costs from the historical cost database to the take-off, adds formwork rental or owned-equipment rates, crane time and winter protection, and enters the totals in the bid summary.

error.defect_description: Productivity rate or wage rate out of date.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; the wait reflects the take-off and pricing spread over several working days between other bids.

steps.name: Review self-perform pricing with operations
steps.description: The director of self-perform operations reviews crew sizes, productivity, sequence, crane and formwork assumptions and any winter work, and adjusts the self-perform price where the field would not meet it.

error.defect_description: Review is a quick look and misses a sequencing problem.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; self-perform contractors check pricing with field operations; spe-director is not a listed role of this process in the organisation file.

steps.name: Price general conditions and duration
steps.description: The estimator builds the site staffing, trailers, hoarding, temporary services, cleanup and winter heat budget from a draft schedule and the site notes, and checks the duration against the owner's completion date and liquidated damages.

error.defect_description: Duration too short for the scope or a winter season missed.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; general conditions priced by time.

steps.name: Submit questions to the consultant
steps.description: The estimator collects questions from the take-off and from trades about conflicts, missing details and substitutions, and submits them in writing through the portal or to the named contact before the question deadline.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: All communications in writing through a single contact; answers only by addendum.

steps.name: Receive addenda
steps.description: The consultant and owner answer bidders' questions and issue addenda on the portal, which sends an automatic notice to registered plan takers. The last major addendum must come out at least five business days before closing.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Addendum timing rules and portal notices from the sources; wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Incorporate addenda
steps.description: The estimator reads each addendum, revises quantities and prices affected, forwards it to trade tendering for the subcontractors, and records the addendum number for acknowledgement on the bid form.

error.defect_description: An addendum change is not carried into the price.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; repeat share of about 30% reflects two or three addenda on a typical tender.

steps.name: Record legal comments and qualifications
steps.description: The lead estimator reads the contracts counsel memo, notes which risk terms must be priced, which can be accepted, and whether the bid must go to executive review; a qualified bid is not allowed, so risk is priced rather than excluded.

error.defect_description: A legal comment is not reflected in contingency.

evidence.note: Qualified bids are rejected, so terms cannot be excluded in the bid; times are estimates.

steps.name: Request the bid bond
steps.description: The bid coordinator fills in the bond request with the owner, project, closing date, estimated bid amount and required bond form, attaching the tender's bid security clause, and sends it to treasury.

error.defect_description: Wrong owner name or bond percentage on the request.

evidence.note: Bid bond of 10% of the bid and agreement to bond on CCDC forms.

steps.name: Approve the bond request
steps.description: The treasury, surety and credit manager checks the bid value against the bonding line and work on hand and sends the request to the surety broker for a digital bid bond and agreement to bond.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Treasury authority over all surety requests (company policy)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; treasury-manager is not a listed role of this process in the organisation file; it is a role of fin-surety-bonding.

steps.name: Receive the bid bond and agreement to bond
steps.description: The surety, through the broker, issues the digital bid bond and agreement to bond in the owner's required form with a verification link. The bid coordinator checks names, amounts and closing date on both.

error.defect_description: Bond issued with a wrong project name or amount.

evidence.note: Digital bonds verified through third-party authentication; wait is an estimate.

steps.name: Draft the bid summary
steps.description: The lead estimator assembles the bid summary sheet: self-perform, general conditions, trade carries with plugs where coverage is thin, allowances, escalation, contingency and fee, and lists the main risks for review.

error.defect_description: A formula or link in the bid summary workbook is broken.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; spreadsheet bid summaries were the norm in 2019-2022.

steps.name: Review the bid strategy with the regional VP
steps.description: The regional vice-president reviews the bid summary, duration, risk register and proposed fee with the chief estimator and decides whether to bid, at what fee range, and whether the bid needs executive review.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Delegation of authority: regional VP approves bids within regional limits

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; about a quarter of stipulated bids above an executive threshold, consistent with the organisation file's 10 executive reviews a month across all bid types.

steps.name: Present the bid at executive review
steps.description: The chief estimator presents the bid summary, contract risks, fee and resourcing to the executive bid review in the last days before closing and records the approved fee floor and conditions.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Executive approval of bids above the threshold set by the board (exec-bid-approval)

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; the organisation file's exec-bid-approval process.

steps.name: Carry levelled trade prices on bid day
steps.description: On closing day the lead and support estimators take the levelled trade prices from trade tendering as they arrive, enter the carried price for each package into the bid summary and watch the trade coverage list for gaps.

error.defect_description: A trade price carried without the addendum or with a scope gap.

evidence.note: Trade bids arrive in the final hours before the deadline; wait is the time until bid day.

steps.name: Set the final price
steps.description: In the last hour the chief estimator reviews the total, compares it with the cost per square metre of similar jobs, makes the final fee and contingency adjustments and fixes the number to submit.

error.defect_description: A last-minute adjustment is keyed in the wrong cell.

control.basis: Chief estimator signs off the final number on every bid

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; final-hour price setting.

steps.name: Complete the bid form and attachments
steps.description: The bid coordinator types the price in words and figures, alternates and separate prices, the list of named subcontractors and the addenda acknowledgements into the bid form, and attaches the bid bond and agreement to bond.

error.defect_description: Addendum not acknowledged, words and figures differ, or a listed subcontractor does not match the carried price.

control.basis: Owner's instructions to bidders: unqualified bid, addenda acknowledged, named subcontractors, bid security on the prescribed form

evidence.note: Bid form contents and rejection grounds from the sources.

steps.name: Check the bid against the checklist
steps.description: A second estimator checks the form against the bid summary and the instructions to bidders: price in words and figures, every addendum, every separate price, bond amount and signatures.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Company bid submission checklist with second-person check

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general contractor estimating practice; error share is an estimate.

steps.name: Upload the bid before closing
steps.description: The bid coordinator uploads the bid form and bond files to the portal, confirms the authority checkbox and receipt time, and keeps the confirmation. Late bids are not accepted.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Tender law and owner rules: bids received after closing are rejected (Nova Scotia guidelines 5.9; Oshawa procedure)

evidence.note: Late and improper bids are rejected; share is an estimate.

steps.name: Record the bid opening results
steps.description: After closing the bid coordinator reads the unofficial results the owner posts on the portal or reads out at the public opening, records all prices and ranks in the CRM and tells the team.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Results posted after closing; low share of about 15% sits in the 1-in-6 to 1-in-10 public hit ratio.

steps.name: Send post-bid documents
steps.description: Within 48 hours the estimator sends the owner what it asks the low bidders for: the list of other subcontractors, price breakouts, safety certification and the schedule of values.

error.defect_description: Breakout does not add to the bid price.

control.basis: Owner's tender conditions: post-bid submissions within 48 hours of opening (Nova Scotia guidelines 6.8)

evidence.note: 48-hour post-bid submission from the source.

steps.name: Check for a bid error on a wide margin
steps.description: The chief estimator compares the company's price with the second bidder; where the gap is large, the team rechecks trade carries and quantities for an omission and decides whether to stand on the bid.
outputs: decision to stand on the bid

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Withdrawal after opening only for a serious demonstrable error within two business days; a bid well below the others warrants scrutiny.

steps.name: Record the result and close the bid file
steps.description: The bid coordinator records competitors' prices and the reason for the loss in the CRM, files the bid and asks for a debriefing where the owner offers one; trade bidders are told by trade tendering.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Bidder debriefing available on request.

exceptions.name: Late addenda
exceptions.description: A second or third addendum changes scope late in the tender period; quantities are revised and trades re-priced, sometimes with a closing extension.

exceptions.name: Executive review
exceptions.description: Bids above the threshold or with unusual terms go to the executive bid review in the last days before closing.

exceptions.name: Bid form error caught
exceptions.description: The second-person check finds an unacknowledged addendum or a mismatch between words and figures, fixed minutes before upload.

exceptions.name: Late or non-compliant bid
exceptions.description: The upload misses the closing time or the bond cannot be verified, and the owner rejects the bid.

exceptions.name: Withdrawal for a serious error
exceptions.description: The company is low by a wide margin, finds an omitted trade and asks to withdraw within two business days.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from go decision to bid result
benchmarks.population: Public stipulated price building tenders in Canada

evidence.note: Author's estimate: tender periods of about three to five weeks with the go decision about a week in; Ontario broader public sector minimum postings of 15 days and 40-day postings under trade agreements (ns2017) bound the range.

benchmarks.population: General contractors, public works (United States averages)

evidence.note: Averages observed across the country; dated.

benchmarks.population: Nova Scotia public sector construction tenders

pain_points.description: Most of the price is trade quotes received in the final hours, so carrying, checking and filling in the form happen in a rush.

evidence.note: Bids often arrive in the final hours or minutes before the deadline.

pain_points.description: Late addenda force re-take-off and re-pricing of trades with little time left.

evidence.note: Addenda allowed up to 3-5 business days before closing.

pain_points.description: A small form error (missing addendum acknowledgement, wrong bond) voids weeks of estimating.

evidence.note: Improper bids are rejected.

pain_points.description: Estimating effort is spent on bids that mostly lose; at one win in six to ten bids, each win carries the cost of the losing bids.

evidence.note: Cost per win equals cost per bid divided by hit rate.

sources.title: Nova Scotia Public Sector Construction Contract Guidelines (June 2017)
sources.supports: Prequalification of bidders with a published minimum score (often 70-80 of 100); solicitation documents list major subcontractors, bid security, CCDC contract form; bonding recommended at $500,000 and over; subcontracts of $250,000 or more should carry contract security; addenda no later than 5 business days (major) or 3 business days (minor) before closing and closing extended at least 1 business day when needed; late bids rejected; amendments and withdrawals allowed up to closing; withdrawal after opening only for serious demonstrable error within 2 business days; within 48 hours of opening bidders may be asked for safety certifications, other subcontractors and price breakouts; bids over the estimate may be negotiated or re-tendered; letter of award binds the contractor to sign; contract security within 10 days of award; bid security of unsuccessful bidders returned within 30 days; international trade agreements may require 40-day postings.

sources.title: Bid Submission Procedure (under Purchasing By-law 80-2020)
sources.supports: Electronic bids only through the bids&tenders system, late bids not accepted; COR, SOSE or ISO 45001 required for construction bids over $500,000; digital bid bond of 10% of the bid and agreement to bond uploaded with the bid on CCDC forms, verified through a third-party authentication firm; qualified bids, unverifiable bonds and improperly executed agreements to bond are rejected; contract documents due within 10 calendar days after written notice of award; acceptance time limit usually 90 days; performance bond of 100%, or 50% performance and 50% labour and material bonds, on award; only the low bidder's references checked; if the low bidder fails to execute, award to the next bidder and forfeit the deposit. PDF metadata shows the file was last saved in July 2021; the copy opened carries a later revision stamp.

sources.title: What Is Bid Leveling in Construction?
sources.supports: Bid leveling steps: log bids, build a scope matrix (included, excluded, alternate, unclear), compare line items, send question lists and document conversations, carry unresolved items conservatively, select on more than price; bids often arrive in the final hours or minutes before the deadline; manual leveling takes 2-4 hours per major scope; a $100M hospital may have 25+ scope packages; a bid 15% below the others warrants scrutiny; ignored qualifications become change orders. Undated vendor page.

sources.title: How is Your 'Bid-Hit' Ratio?
sources.publisher: Mason Contractors Association of America (George Hedley)
sources.supports: Average general contractor bid-hit ratios: public works 6:1 to 10:1, private bid work 4:1 to 6:1, negotiated and design-build work 2:1 to 4:1; ratios above 11:1 on public work cost too much in estimating; tracking ratios by job type, customer and competitors guides which jobs to pursue.

sources.title: Bid management in construction: what it is and why it decides your win rate
sources.supports: Illustration of 20 estimator hours per bid at $75 loaded ($1,500 per bid); cost per win equals cost per bid divided by hit rate; survey of more than 2,000 contractors found fewer than 10% knew their bid-hit ratio; a bid/no-bid screen on customer history, fit, capacity, competition and risk before opening drawings.

assumptions: The process runs from the go decision to the bid result; trade solicitation and levelling (bd-trade-tendering), legal review, bonding and executive approval are separate processes and appear here only as handoffs.
The bid is a public tender for a $5M to $40M building; private invited stipulated tenders follow the same steps with fewer formal rules.
Waits include days when the bid sits between bursts of work while estimators work on other bids that close the same week.
Low-bidder share of 15% is set within the 1-in-6 to 1-in-10 public hit ratio (hedley2008); a US source from 2008, so a tier C fit for Canada 2019-2022.
Estimator FTE covers only this process's steps; trade solicitation and levelling for the same bids is counted in bd-trade-tendering.
Role costs and titles from the organisation file; spe-director and treasury-manager are organisation file roles that the process map does not list for this process.
No equipment, vehicles or crews are tied up; the site visit is a travel step in a personal or pool car.
